name: Confuses number of groups with group size
description: Interchanges how many groups there are with how many items are in each group when interpreting multiplication or division.
evidenceSignals: Uses 3 groups of 4 and 4 groups of 3 interchangeably when the context distinguishes them.
Labels the divisor or quotient with the wrong contextual role.

name: Treats division only as sharing
description: Recognises partitive sharing but does not recognise grouping or quotative division as the same division structure.
evidenceSignals: Can split 12 objects among 3 children but cannot answer how many groups of 3 fit in 12.

name: Does not connect multiplication and division
description: Treats multiplication and division facts as unrelated procedures rather than inverse relationships in one fact family.
evidenceSignals: Knows 4 × 5 = 20 but cannot use it to determine 20 ÷ 5.

name: Multiplication fact retrieval error
description: Makes an isolated or repeated multiplication-fact recall error despite representing the operation and grouping structure correctly; keep distinct from a concept misconception.
evidenceSignals: Draws the correct equal groups or array but recalls the numerical product incorrectly.

name: Larger denominator means larger fraction
description: Compares denominator numerals as whole numbers and ignores that a larger denominator means smaller equal parts for the same whole.
evidenceSignals: Claims 1/8 is greater than 1/4 because 8 is greater than 4.

name: Compares numerators only
description: Chooses the larger numerator without considering denominator or common whole.
evidenceSignals: Claims 3/8 is greater than 2/3 because 3 is greater than 2.

name: Changes only one part of an equivalent fraction
description: Multiplies or divides only the numerator or only the denominator when trying to form an equivalent fraction.
evidenceSignals: Changes 1/2 to 1/4 or 2/2 after applying a factor to only one term.

name: Confuses part size with number of equal parts
description: Does not coordinate the number of equal parts with the size of each part in a fixed whole.
evidenceSignals: Expects eighths to be larger pieces than fourths because there are more parts.
